items.claim: L-BFGS overwrites its oldest step before rejecting the new one
`unwarpPoint` diverges once a pin warp turns the shape past 60°, and returns its last guess rather than its best
items.note: It now takes Newton steps through a central-difference Jacobian, halves a step until it shrinks the miss, and returns the best point found.

items.claim: Dragging a second pin that shares an outline vertex with an earlier pin does nothing
items.note: Pins sharing a vertex move it by the mean of their drags. I made that call myself and recorded it in `docs/unruled.md`. It does not throw, because two pins snapping to one point is ordinary input.

items.claim: A pinned vertex that refine leaves out of every triangle never reaches its target
items.note: The real cause was in `refine.ts`: `legalize` popped stale stack entries and flipped with the wrong corner, which deleted triangles. A random decagon's mesh covered 7345 of its 9190 units of area. The corner is now read from the triangle that holds the edge. Refine also inserts any point earcut left out, and `pinWarpMesh` marks a pin `-1` when no triangle holds its point.

items.claim: An even-odd self-crossing outline is meshed as if it did not cross
`meshLocator` stops at ring 1 without the bound its comment promises
items.note: It now ranks candidates by distance to the triangle instead of by weight, and keeps widening the search until no unseen triangle can be nearer.

items.claim: A piece with two or more pins whose system fails to factor ignores its own pins
items.note: Such a piece now follows the rigid fit to its own pins.
